### Cloud provider

            <thead>

                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="google_dns_managed_zone_name" href="#google_dns_managed_zone_name">google_dns_managed_zone_name</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>GCP DNS zone name to automatically manage DNS entries.</p>
<p>Leave it empty to manage it manually.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="google_kubernetes_storage_class" href="#google_kubernetes_storage_class">google_kubernetes_storage_class</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>GCP Kubernetes Storage Class to use for datastores and Prometheus persistent volumes.
See https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/persistent-disks#disk-types for more details and
available options.</p>
<p>Depending on your use case, performance may be significantly improved with higher-tier storage classes, though this should be balanced against the associated costs.</p>
<p>Both CockroachDB and YugabyteDB recommend SSDs for production workloads, configured via the <code>premium-rwo</code> storage class. Use <code>standard</code> for testing only.</p>
<p>See https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.1/recommended-production-settings#gcp and https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/deploy/checklist/#google-cloud for database-specific recommendations.</p>
<p>Example: <code>premium-rwo</code> for production and <code>standard</code> for development.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="google_machine_type" href="#google_machine_type">google_machine_type</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>GCP machine type used for the Kubernetes node pool.
See https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-resource for more details and available options.</p>
<p>Depending on your use case, performance may be significantly improved with higher-tier instances, though this should be balanced against the associated costs.</p>
<p>Both CockroachDB and YugabyteDB recommend <code>n2</code> instances for production. Use <code>f1</code> and <code>g1</code> instances for testing only.</p>
<p>See https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v24.1/recommended-production-settings#gcp and https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable/deploy/checklist/#google-cloud for database-specific recommendations.</p>
<p>Example: <code>n2-standard-4</code> for production, <code>e2-medium</code> for development.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="google_preshared_cert" href="#google_preshared_cert">google_preshared_cert</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Name of a pre-shared SSL certificate of the Google Cloud project, used by the DSS gateway
instead of a Google-managed certificate. A Google-managed certificate is used when empty.</p>
<p>Details on generation are available there:
https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/secure-traffic-management#pre-shared-certificates</p>
<p>Example: <code>dss-certificate</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="google_project_name" href="#google_project_name">google_project_name</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>Name of the GCP project hosting the future cluster</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="google_zone" href="#google_zone">google_zone</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>GCP zone hosting the kubernetes cluster
List of available zones: https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones#available</p>
<p>Example: <code>europe-west6-a</code></p>
</td>
                </tr></tbody>

### Core service

<table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Variable</th>
                    <th>Type</th>
                    <th>Default</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody><tr>
                    <td><a id="authorization" href="#authorization">authorization</a></td>
                    <td><code>object({<br/>public_key_pem_path = optional(string),<br/> jwks = optional(object({<br/>endpoint = string,<br/> key_id = string,<br/> refresh_interval = optional(string),<br/> key_ttl = optional(string)})<br/>)})<br/></code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>One of <code>public_key_pem_path</code> or <code>jwks</code> should be provided but not both.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>public_key_pem_path
If providing the access token public key via JWKS, do not provide this parameter.
If providing a .pem file directly as the public key to validate incoming access tokens, specify the name
of this .pem file here as /public-certs/YOUR-KEY-NAME.pem replacing YOUR-KEY-NAME as appropriate. For instance,
if using the provided us-demo.pem, use the path /public-certs/us-demo.pem. Note that your .pem file should be built
in the docker image or mounted manually.</p>
<p>Example 1 (dummy auth):</p>
<pre><code>{
  public_key_pem_path = &quot;/test-certs/auth2.pem&quot;
}
</code></pre>
<p>Example 2:</p>
<pre><code>{
  public_key_pem_path = &quot;/jwt-public-certs/us-demo.pem&quot;
}
</code></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>jwks
If providing a .pem file directly as the public key to validate incoming access tokens, do not provide this parameter.</p>
<ul>
<li>endpoint
If providing the access token public key via JWKS, specify the JWKS endpoint here.
Example: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json</li>
<li>key_id:
If providing the access token public key via JWKS, specify the kid (key ID) of they appropriate key in the JWKS file referenced above.</li>
<li>refresh_interval:
Cadence at which the keys are fetched again from the JWKS endpoint. Defaults to the core-service default when omitted.
Example: 1m</li>
<li>key_ttl:
Duration during which keys that could not be refreshed are still used before the core-service shuts down.
Defaults to the core-service default when omitted.
Example: 1h
Example:</li>
</ul>
<pre><code>{
  jwks = {
    endpoint = &quot;https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json&quot;
    key_id = &quot;9C6DF78B-77A7-4E89-8990-E654841A7826&quot;
    refresh_interval = &quot;1m&quot;
    key_ttl = &quot;1h&quot;
  }
}
</code></pre>
</li>
</ul>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="core_service_cpu_limit" href="#core_service_cpu_limit">core_service_cpu_limit</a></td>

                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="image_pull_secret" href="#image_pull_secret">image_pull_secret</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Secret name of the credentials to access the image registry.
If the image specified in <code>VAR_DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME</code> requires
authentication, you can use the following command to store the credentials as secrets:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>kubectl create secret -n VAR_NAMESPACE docker-registry VAR_DOCKER_IMAGE_PULL_SECRET <br />
--docker-server=DOCKER_REGISTRY_SERVER <br />
--docker-username=DOCKER_USER <br />
--docker-password=DOCKER_PASSWORD <br />
--docker-email=DOCKER_EMAIL</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Replace <code>VAR_DOCKER_IMAGE_PULL_SECRET</code> with the secret name (for instance: <code>private-registry-credentials</code>).
For docker hub private repository, use <code>docker.io</code> as <code>DOCKER_REGISTRY_SERVER</code> and an
<a href="https://hub.docker.com/settings/security">access token</a> as <code>DOCKER_PASSWORD</code>.</p>
<p>Example: docker-registry</p>
</td>

                    <td><code>string</code></td>

<p>Example: &lt;ORGNAME_CLUSTER_NAME&gt;</p>
</td>

### CockroachDB

<table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Variable</th>
                    <th>Type</th>
                    <th>Default</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_cache" href="#crdb_cache">crdb_cache</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"25%"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Size of the CockroachDB storage engine cache, passed to the <code>--cache</code> flag of <code>cockroach start</code>.
Either a percentage of the memory available to the container or an absolute size.</p>
<p>Example: <code>25%</code> or <code>2GiB</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_cluster_name" href="#crdb_cluster_name">crdb_cluster_name</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>A string that specifies a CRDB cluster name. This is used together to ensure that all newly created
nodes join the intended cluster when you are running multiple clusters.
The CRDB cluster is automatically given a randomly-generated name if an empty string is provided.
The CRDB cluster name must be 6-20 characters in length, and can include lowercase letters, numbers,
and dashes (but no leading or trailing dashes). A cluster's name cannot be edited after it is created.</p>
<p>Example: interuss-us-production</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_cpu_limit" href="#crdb_cpu_limit">crdb_cpu_limit</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Kubernetes CPU limit of the CockroachDB containers.
Not set by default.</p>
<p>Example: <code>3.5</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_cpu_request" href="#crdb_cpu_request">crdb_cpu_request</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Kubernetes CPU request of the CockroachDB containers.
Not set by default.</p>
<p>Example: <code>3.5</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_enable_liveness_probe" href="#crdb_enable_liveness_probe">crdb_enable_liveness_probe</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this boolean false to replace the CockroachDB liveness probe by a probe that always succeeds. See https://github.com/interuss/dss/issues/1732 for potential reasons to do so.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_enable_readiness_probe" href="#crdb_enable_readiness_probe">crdb_enable_readiness_probe</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this boolean false to replace the CockroachDB readiness probe by a probe that always succeeds. See https://github.com/interuss/dss/issues/1732 for potential reasons to do so.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_env" href="#crdb_env">crdb_env</a></td>
                    <td><code>map(string)</code></td>
                    <td><code>{}</code></td>
                    <td><p>Additional environment variables of the CockroachDB containers, for instance to tune the Go runtime.</p>
<p>Example: <code>{ GOGC = &quot;80&quot;, GOMAXPROCS = &quot;2&quot; }</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_external_nodes" href="#crdb_external_nodes">crdb_external_nodes</a></td>
                    <td><code>list(string)</code></td>
                    <td><code>[]</code></td>
                    <td><p>Fully-qualified domain name of existing CRDB nodes outside of the cluster if you are joining an existing pool.
Example: [&quot;0.db.dss.example.com&quot;, &quot;1.db.dss.example.com&quot;, &quot;2.db.dss.example.com&quot;]</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_image_tag" href="#crdb_image_tag">crdb_image_tag</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><em>Required</em></td>
                    <td><p>Version tag of the CockroachDB image.
Until v.16, the recommended CockroachDB version is v21.2.7.
From v.17, the recommended CockroachDB version is v24.1.3.</p>
<p>Example: v24.1.3</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_max_sql_memory" href="#crdb_max_sql_memory">crdb_max_sql_memory</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"25%"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Maximum memory CockroachDB can use for SQL queries, passed to the <code>--max-sql-memory</code> flag of <code>cockroach start</code>.
Either a percentage of the memory available to the container or an absolute size.</p>
<p>Example: <code>25%</code> or <code>2GiB</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_memory_limit" href="#crdb_memory_limit">crdb_memory_limit</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Kubernetes memory limit of the CockroachDB containers.
Not set by default.</p>
<p>Example: <code>14Gi</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="crdb_memory_request" href="#crdb_memory_request">crdb_memory_request</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Kubernetes memory request of the CockroachDB containers.
Not set by default.</p>
<p>Example: <code>14Gi</code></p>
</td>
                </tr></tbody>
        </table>

### YugabyteDB

<table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Variable</th>
                    <th>Type</th>
                    <th>Default</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody><tr>
                    <td><a id="yugabyte_cloud" href="#yugabyte_cloud">yugabyte_cloud</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"dss"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Cloud of yugabyte instances, used for partionning.</p>
<p>Should be set to dss unless you're doing advanced partitionning.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="yugabyte_external_nodes" href="#yugabyte_external_nodes">yugabyte_external_nodes</a></td>
                    <td><code>list(string)</code></td>
                    <td><code>[]</code></td>
                    <td><p>Fully-qualified domain name of existing yugabyte master nodes outside of the cluster if you are joining an existing pool.
Example: [&quot;0.master.db.dss.example.com&quot;, &quot;1.master.db.dss.example.com&quot;, &quot;2.master.db.dss.example.com&quot;]</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="yugabyte_light_resources" href="#yugabyte_light_resources">yugabyte_light_resources</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>false</code></td>
                    <td><p>Enable light resources reservation for yugabyte instances.</p>
<p>Useful for a dev cluster when you don't want to overload your kubernetes cluster.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="yugabyte_region" href="#yugabyte_region">yugabyte_region</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"uss-1"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Region of yugabyte instances, used for partionning.</p>
<p>Should be different from others USS in a cluster.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="yugabyte_zone" href="#yugabyte_zone">yugabyte_zone</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"zone"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Zone of yugabyte instances, used for partionning.</p>
<p>Should be set to zone unless you're doing advanced partitionning.</p>
</td>
                </tr></tbody>
        </table>

### Raft

<table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Variable</th>
                    <th>Type</th>
                    <th>Default</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody><tr>
                    <td><a id="raft_automatic_bootstrap" href="#raft_automatic_bootstrap">raft_automatic_bootstrap</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>false</code></td>
                    <td><p>Form the Raft groups automatically: the first node of this instance bootstraps them, then the other nodes of
this instance and the nodes of <code>raft_automatic_bootstrap_nodes</code> are added to them one at a time, retrying until
all of them are members.</p>
<p>Only meant for automation: enable it only for the first nodes of a cluster, otherwise independent Raft groups
are created.</p>
<p>Only used with the raft datastore.</p>
<p>Example: <code>true</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="raft_automatic_bootstrap_nodes" href="#raft_automatic_bootstrap_nodes">raft_automatic_bootstrap_nodes</a></td>
                    <td><code>list(string)</code></td>
                    <td><code>[]</code></td>
                    <td><p>Addresses (host:port, no scheme) of the Raft listeners of the nodes of other participants to add to the Raft
groups with <code>raft_automatic_bootstrap</code>.</p>
<p>Only used with the raft datastore.</p>
<p>Example: <code>[&quot;0.raft.dss.example.com:2407&quot;, &quot;1.raft.dss.example.com:2407&quot;]</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="raft_cluster_id" href="#raft_cluster_id">raft_cluster_id</a></td>
                    <td><code>number</code></td>
                    <td><code>1</code></td>
                    <td><p>Raft cluster ID. Must be identical on all nodes of the pool.</p>
<p>Only used with the raft datastore.</p>
<p>Example: <code>1</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="raft_port" href="#raft_port">raft_port</a></td>
                    <td><code>number</code></td>
                    <td><code>2407</code></td>
                    <td><p>Port of the Raft listener of the nodes of this instance.</p>
<p>Only used with the raft datastore.</p>
<p>Example: <code>2407</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="raft_storage_size" href="#raft_storage_size">raft_storage_size</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"100Gi"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Size of the persistent volume of each Raft node.</p>
<p>Only used with the raft datastore.</p>
<p>Example: <code>100Gi</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="raft_tls_secret" href="#raft_tls_secret">raft_tls_secret</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"dss.raft.certs"</code></td>
                    <td><p>Name of the Kubernetes secret holding the mutual TLS material of the Raft listeners:
<code>node.raft-&lt;i&gt;.crt</code>/<code>node.raft-&lt;i&gt;.key</code> is the certificate of the pod of ordinal <code>&lt;i&gt;</code> of this instance,
<code>ca.crt</code> is the PEM bundle of the CAs of every participant of the pool, including its own.</p>
<p>Only used with the raft datastore.</p>
<p>Example: <code>dss.raft.certs</code></p>
</td>
                </tr></tbody>
        </table>

### Cleanup

<table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Variable</th>
                    <th>Type</th>
                    <th>Default</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_enable_rid_cron" href="#evict_enable_rid_cron">evict_enable_rid_cron</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this to true to enable the cron job that automatically cleanup RID entries.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_enable_scd_cron" href="#evict_enable_scd_cron">evict_enable_scd_cron</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>false</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this to true to enable the cron job that automatically cleanup expired SCD entries.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_batch_size" href="#evict_rid_batch_size">evict_rid_batch_size</a></td>
                    <td><code>number</code></td>
                    <td><code>0</code></td>
                    <td><p>Number of entities deleted per batch query (per type) by each run of the RID eviction command.
Set to 0 to delete all expired entities in a single query (per type).</p>
<p>Example: <code>100</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_isas" href="#evict_rid_isas">evict_rid_isas</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this to true to enable cleanup of RID ISAs.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_limit" href="#evict_rid_limit">evict_rid_limit</a></td>
                    <td><code>number</code></td>
                    <td><code>0</code></td>
                    <td><p>Maximum number of entities deleted by each run of the RID eviction command.
Set to 0 to delete all expired entities in a single run.</p>
<p>Example: <code>1000</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_schedule" href="#evict_rid_schedule">evict_rid_schedule</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>When the RID cleanup job shall be performed; expressed in cron format (https://crontab.guru/).
Leave empty to run hourly at a minute deterministically derived from the locality.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_subscriptions" href="#evict_rid_subscriptions">evict_rid_subscriptions</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this to true to enable cleanup of RID subscriptions.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_timeout" href="#evict_rid_timeout">evict_rid_timeout</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Timeout of the RID eviction command; expressed in Go duration format (https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).
Leave empty to use the default value of the command.</p>
<p>Example: <code>10m</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_rid_ttl" href="#evict_rid_ttl">evict_rid_ttl</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"30m"</code></td>
                    <td><p>How long expired RID items should stay before being automatically removed; expressed in Go duration format (https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_batch_size" href="#evict_scd_batch_size">evict_scd_batch_size</a></td>
                    <td><code>number</code></td>
                    <td><code>0</code></td>
                    <td><p>Number of entities deleted per batch query (per type) by each run of the SCD eviction command.
Set to 0 to delete all expired entities in a single query (per type).</p>
<p>Example: <code>100</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_limit" href="#evict_scd_limit">evict_scd_limit</a></td>
                    <td><code>number</code></td>
                    <td><code>0</code></td>
                    <td><p>Maximum number of entities deleted by each run of the SCD eviction command.
Set to 0 to delete all expired entities in a single run.</p>
<p>Example: <code>1000</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_operational_intents" href="#evict_scd_operational_intents">evict_scd_operational_intents</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this to true to enable cleanup of SCD operational intents.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_schedule" href="#evict_scd_schedule">evict_scd_schedule</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>When the SCD cleanup job shall be performed; expressed in cron format (https://crontab.guru/).
Leave empty to run daily at 2 AM at a minute deterministically derived from the locality.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_subscriptions" href="#evict_scd_subscriptions">evict_scd_subscriptions</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>true</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set this to true to enable cleanup of SCD subscriptions.</p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_timeout" href="#evict_scd_timeout">evict_scd_timeout</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>""</code></td>
                    <td><p>Timeout of the SCD eviction command; expressed in Go duration format (https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).
Leave empty to use the default value of the command.</p>
<p>Example: <code>10m</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="evict_scd_ttl" href="#evict_scd_ttl">evict_scd_ttl</a></td>
                    <td><code>string</code></td>
                    <td><code>"2688h"</code></td>
                    <td><p>How long expired SCD items should stay before being automatically removed; expressed in Go duration format (https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).</p>
</td>
                </tr></tbody>
        </table>

### Monitoring

<table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Variable</th>
                    <th>Type</th>
                    <th>Default</th>
                    <th>Description</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody><tr>
                    <td><a id="alerting" href="#alerting">alerting</a></td>
                    <td><code>object({<br/>smtp_smarthost = string,<br/> smtp_email = string,<br/> smtp_password = string,<br/> dest = string})<br/></code></td>
                    <td><code>null</code></td>
                    <td><p>Alerting by email with Alertmanager. Alerting is disabled when not set.</p>
<ul>
<li>smtp_smarthost: SMTP server, with its port.</li>
<li>smtp_email: Email address sending the alerts, also used to authenticate on the SMTP server.</li>
<li>smtp_password: Password to authenticate on the SMTP server.</li>
<li>dest: Email address receiving the alerts.</li>
</ul>
<p>Example:</p>
<pre><code>{
  smtp_smarthost     = &quot;smtp.example.com:587&quot;
  smtp_email         = &quot;dss@example.com&quot;
  smtp_password      = &quot;password&quot;
  dest               = &quot;team@example.com&quot;
}
</code></pre>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="enable_dss_metrics" href="#enable_dss_metrics">enable_dss_metrics</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>false</code></td>
                    <td><p>Enable DSS's prometheus metric.</p>
<p>Require DSS version to be at least 0.23.0.</p>
<p>Example: <code>true</code></p>
</td>
                </tr><tr>
                    <td><a id="enable_monitoring" href="#enable_monitoring">enable_monitoring</a></td>
                    <td><code>bool</code></td>
                    <td><code>false</code></td>
                    <td><p>Set to true to enable monitoring stack with prometheus / grafana.</p>
<p>Example: <code>true</code></p>
</td>
                </tr></tbody>
        </table>
